headlines.article_text: Neocloud stocks drop after Microsoft revises capex down Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points CoreWeave, Nebius and IREN fell as Microsoft's lower-than-expected capex figure points to infrastructure partners taking longer to deliver capacity. It's been a rocky past few weeks for neoclouds on concern that rising interest rates will make their buildouts too costly. However, the group had bounced back this week, boosted by some positive analyst comments. Yuki Iwamura | Bloomberg | Getty Images Shares of neoclouds like CoreWeave and Nebius dropped in extended trading as Microsoft's lower-than-expected capital expenditures figure points to infrastructure partners taking longer to deliver data center capacity. Microsoft on Wednesday reported $45.2 billion worth of capex and finance leases during the quarter, up about 30% from a year earlier, but below the $50.7 billion average analyst estimate, according to StreetAccount. Microsoft is particularly reliant on neoclouds for capacity as it pours money into its artificial intelligence infrastructure. Microsoft inked a nearly $20 billion deal with Nebius at the tail end of last year for compute through the 2030s. It's also a top customer for CoreWeave. Those companies and their peers have experienced a rocky few weeks on the market as rising interest rates led to concerns that future debt raises will be too expensive and lenders will start retreating. In its earnings report, Microsoft said Azure revenue jumped 48% from a year earlier, far outpacing the increase in capex. "Growth was higher than capital expenditures driven by timing differences between receipt of goods and payment and a lower mix of finance leases," Microsoft said its earnings deck. CoreWeave and Nebius slid almost 5% after Microsoft's report. IREN fell about 3%. Alphabet on Wednesday also reported capex numbers that fell short of estimates. The Google parent's capex totaled $51.36 billion, while analysts expected $55.09 billion. SpaceX CEO Elon Musk , whose company rents AI infrastructure to Anthropic and Google , predicted over the weekend that more than 200 neocloud companies will collapse, posting on X that "debt markets have almost entirely shut off access to money for any company that doesn't have substantial revenue independent of AI data centers." And last Monday, analysts at Gartner shared with CNBC its prediction that, by 2030, 80% of neocloud companies will either be absorbed or completely cease operations. After a steep plunge this month, the neoclouds had been enjoying a modest recovery this week, with CoreWeave up 18% in the past three trading days to pace the gains. Analysts at Wolfe Research wrote in a report on Tuesday that they see the stock rebounding into the mid-$70s. It closed Wednesday at $63.93. The infrastructure story gained some strength earlier on Wednesday as Oracle issued a strong long-term revenue forecast and said it will return to being free cash flow positive in the second half of next fiscal year. The stock jumped 11% in regular trading before retreating 3% following Microsoft's report. —CNBC's Jordan Novet contributed to this report. headlines.article_text: DoorDash's deal to buy Instacart coming as early as Thursday morning, sources tell CNBC Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points DoorDash's bid to buy Instacart could be announced as early as Thursday morning, CNBC has learned. In this article DASH Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT watch now VIDEO 1:02 01:02 DoorDash deal to buy Instacart to be announced as early as Thursday morning Closing Bell: Overtime DoorDash 's bid to buy Instacart could be announced as soon as Thursday morning, sources familiar with the matter told CNBC. Speculation of a deal has swirled since last week, when The Information reported Instacart was exploring a sale and had held talks with companies including Uber and DoorDash. On Monday, several outlets reported DoorDash was in advanced discussions to acquire Instacart and that the deal could value Instacart at about $17 billion. Instacart's stock popped about 4% in extended trading on Wednesday, while DoorDash shares fell less than 1%. Instacart declined to comment. Representatives from DoorDash didn't immediately respond to CNBC's request for comment. Acquiring Instacart would give DoorDash a bigger presence in online grocery delivery. DoorDash got its start in food delivery, and since then it has added more retailers to its marketplace, such as Sephora, Macy's , Staples and Anthropologie. In recent months, it's brought on a growing stable of regional grocers, after announcing a partnership with Kroger last year. Instacart , which went public in 2023, was one of the biggest beneficiaries of a pandemic-driven surge in grocery delivery services, but it has struggled to maintain that momentum. In December Instacart agreed to pay $60 million to settle allegations by the Federal Trade Commission that it misled users with false advertising and deployed "unlawful subscription enrollment" practices. The service has also faced increasingly stiff competition from companies like Amazon and Walmart . After slowing its brick-and-mortar grocery effort, Amazon has doubled down on its online grocery business and leveraged its vast fulfillment footprint to speed up deliveries of household essentials, pantry staples and perishables. Both Amazon and Walmart have pushed further into same- and next-day delivery, which poses a threat to Instacart's on-demand delivery model. Analysts have noted that a potential combination of Instacart and DoorDash could attract antitrust scrutiny given the companies' market overlap. Third-party delivery platforms "remain a minority of total grocery consumption, but slicing and dicing the online market more narrowly or from a perspective of the grocers as enterprise customers can make approvals more challenging," Wedbush analysts wrote in a Monday research note. headlines.article_text: Hands-on with Apple's first touchscreen laptop Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points Apple announced its first touchscreen laptop models on Wednesday at an event in Los Angeles. Here's the good news for anyone who is worried about the new user interface: You don't have to use it. Apple said it used an oleophobic coating on its screens to resist fingerprints. It appears to work. In this article AAPL Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT watch now VIDEO 1:59 01:59 Apple's new touchscreen Macbook Pro — first impressions News Videos Apple announced its first touchscreen laptop models on Wednesday at an event in Los Angeles. These new MacBooks, called MacBook Pro with ProLED XDR Display, are still Apple MacBooks. They run MacOS, not iPadOS or iOS, the iPhone's operating system. Here's the good news for anyone who is worried about the new user interface: You don't have to use it. Touch is entirely optional. CNBC briefly tested both the 14-inch and 16-inch touchscreen MacBooks at the event. Users can still primarily or entirely use the device's trackpad and keyboard, and there are few visual updates. MacOS still looks largely the same as it used to. Apple's touchscreen MacBook Pro with ProLED XDR Display. Andrew Evers | CNBC There have been a few user interface updates. For example, the red button on the top left of a window expands when you touch it to make it easier to click. Apple says that third-party developers like Microsoft and Adobe can and will update their apps to expand buttons and other touch targets to be larger. I think that touch will be particularly useful to scroll through websites or documents while lying down. But even software that hasn't been explicitly updated for the new computer will support touch. Apple says that behind the scenes, its software converts every touch tap into a traditional click. So any button that can be clicked can also be touched. Using the laptop with your finger feels good, but it won't change the way most people use their laptops. It could be useful for iPhone app developers, who can now test the way their apps work on their Mac. An accessibility feature allows users to pinch to zoom on any part of the user interface. Apple said on Wednesday that it had used an oleophobic coating on its screens to resist fingerprints. It appears to work. I didn't notice marks on the screen when I used the touch features. Apple is also, in addition to the touch feature, marketing these laptops as having a superior display, thanks to its new tandem OLED technology that offers deeper blacks and higher contrast. While photos and other art looked great on the screen, it's not a night-and-day difference from past Apple laptops. A lot of the improvements are aimed at creators who need accurate colors for photo and video editing. Apple's touchscreen MacBook Pro with ProLED XDR Display and 12MP Center Stage camera. Andrew Evers | CNBC Instead of the notch at the top of previous MacBooks, where Apple hides its cameras, the new MacBooks have a hole-punch cutout in the display, like recent iPhones. Apple's Dynamic Island feature — new to the MacBook — expands to show live activities and Siri. Apple made a big deal about the laptop's new hinge, which is meant to keep the screen from shaking when you touch it. For example, if you tap the screen on a video call, your camera won't shake as much. But the hinge feels largely the same as Apple's previous MacBook Pros. There is one new feature that is immediately noticeable and tells people you bought the latest, greatest, and most expensive Apple laptop. (The smaller 14-inch model starts at $2,899 and the bigger one costs at least $3,399.) The Apple logo on the lid now lights up when the computer is on. It's the first Apple laptop that supports it since the 2017 MacBook Air. Apple’s new touchscreen MacBook Pro. Andrew Evers | CNBC The light-up logo drew a cheer from analysts and influencers in attendance when it was announced on Wednesday. headlines.article_text: Microsoft (MSFT) Q1 earnings report 2027 Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points Microsoft reported 19% revenue growth, topping estimates. Dimitar Dilkoff | AFP | Getty Images Microsoft shares rose 4% in extended trading on Wednesday after the company reported better-than-expected quarterly results, driven by 48% growth in its Azure cloud infrastructure business. Here's how the company fared relative to LSEG consensus: Earnings per share: $4.89 adjusted vs. $4.73 expected Revenue: $92.28 billion vs. $90.69 billion expected Microsoft's revenue grew 19% year over year in the quarter, which ended on Sept. 30, according to a statement , with Azure now its biggest single business. The software giant has been rapidly building out data center infrastructure to meet artificial intelligence demand, while also maintaining positive free cash flow unlike its fellow hyperscalers. Microsoft reported $45.2 billion worth of capital expenditures and finance leases during the quarter, up about 30% from a year earlier. Analysts surveyed by StreetAccount had projected $50.67 billion. With respect to guidance, Microsoft called for $96 billion to $97.1 billion in fiscal second-quarter revenue, which works out to 18.8% growth at the middle of the range. Analysts polled by LSEG had predicted $95.60 billion in revenue. For Azure, Hood said she anticipates 49% to 50% growth at constant currency for the fiscal second quarter, compared with the 45.1% StreetAccount consensus. "We still have demand that exceeds supply," she said. During the fiscal first quarter, Microsoft flagged a higher growth rate for cash paid for property and equipment than overall capital expenditures, which include finance leases. "Some third-party capacity deliveries we expected in Q1 were delayed," the company's finance chief, Amy Hood, said on a conference call with analysts. Around 75% of capital expenditures are now tied to short-lived assets such as Intel chips and Nvidia graphics processing units, up from about 66% in the past three quarters and half in the year-ago quarter. The shift indicates Microsoft's prioritization of infrastructure it can can quickly turn into revenue. Hood said the company is aiming at over $50 billion in fiscal second-quarter capital expenditures and finance leases, above the StreetAccount consensus of $53.10 billion, with $170 billion for all of calendar 2027 because of the capacity issues. "In the second half of the fiscal year, we currently expect capex spend to accelerate primarily from CPUs, inclusive of higher memory and storage costs, and GPUs, as well as the 3P capacity deliveries that shifted to H2," she said. The delays have to do with GPU-as-a-service providers, she said. Free cash flow for the fiscal first quarter declined 27% to $18.63 billion. Cloud rival Alphabet reported more than $9 billion in negative free cash flow in the quarter after Meta said last week its cash flow turned negative for the first time. Microsoft will continue to generate free cash flow through the 2027 fiscal year, but the company will access additional sources of funding when it's attractive to do so, Hood said. But the burrito chain saw traffic and same-store sales grow during the quarter as low-income consumers spent more, bucking industry trends, and CEO Scott Boatwright projected a strong finish to the year. Shares of the company rose 7% in extended trading. "Broader consumer and industry headwinds may continue, but initiatives across our recipe for growth strategy are building and giving us more tools to win in any environment," Boatwright said on the company's earnings conference call. "We are still in the early stages of this work, and it's gaining traction." Like the broader restaurant industry, Chipotle saw trends soften in early October, although executives said its traffic has returned to growth since then. Boatwright said the company has "high confidence" in its performance for the rest of the fourth quarter. "We feel very confident that November and December set up very well for us," Boatwright said. The company's restaurant-level operating margin fell from 24.5% to 23.3%. Excluding restaurant asset impairment charges and stock-based compensation, the company earned 27 cents per share. Net sales rose 9.6% to $3.29 billion, fueled by the chain's new restaurants. During the quarter, Chipotle opened 84 company-owned restaurants and five international locations run by licensees. In the second half of July, Chipotle said it started to see sales pull back as diners grew concerned about consuming raw lettuce due to cyclospora, although its own supply was never tied to an outbreak. Then in August, the chain disclosed that it had temporarily pulled jalapenos from Minnesota restaurants after learning its supply was potentially linked to a salmonella outbreak. Still, the chain was able to report same-store sales growth for its third straight quarter, shaking off last year's traffic woes. For the first time this year, low-income consumers during the quarter outperformed the high-income cohort at its restaurants, Boatwright said. And discounts aren't the reason — low-income consumers spent the most in September, when promotions were at their low point during the quarter, he told analysts. For the full year, Chipotle reiterated its previous forecast that its same-store sales will increase by a low-single-digit percentage. The laptop market has been going through one of its worst slumps ever. Overall shipments are expected to be down 11% this year. Analysts say the AI-driven global market shortage of memory has contributed to higher laptop prices, which has hurt sales and demand. In the third quarter, total PC shipments dropped 20% on a year-over-year basis, according to market researcher IDC. Apple's own shipments fell 11% during the quarter, according to the estimate. Even Apple's not immune to rising memory prices, after then-CEO Tim Cook warned this summer that the situation around memory prices was "unsustainable." Nearly all Macs got price hikes this year. Mac Minis introduced in August got a $300 bump, for example. The announcement caps a busy two months of product launches under Ternus. Apple also introduced new iMac and MacBook Pro models with M6 chips this week, after price hikes to the lineup totaling several hundred dollars in June. Apple introduced an iPad Mini on Monday that starts at $699, $100 more than its predecessor. Attendees try out the new touchscreen MacBook Pro during the Apple Experience LA in Los Angeles, Oct. 28, 2026. Frederic J. Brown | AFP | Getty Images In September, Apple released new iPhones, including its first foldable phone, the iPhone Duo. It also revealed a new smart speaker with a display called HomeView that uses a redesigned version of Siri to answer a broader range of questions. The launch signifies the growing strategic importance of the Mac to Apple, despite it generating less revenue than the iPhone. In the most recent quarter, Apple reported $10.35 billion in Mac sales, or just under 10% of the company's total revenue. But many software developers swear by the Mac, and it remains the only supported platform to develop iPhone apps. And in recent months, Apple has highlighted its chips and memory architecture to make the case that its computers are the best fit for local or edge AI that runs on a device, instead of the cloud. Meta's AI model developer team bought hundreds of Mac Minis this year to test agents, for example. And Apple notably teamed up with Meta earlier this month to make an announcement that large, nearly frontier models can run on clusters of Macs connected with high-speed cabling, allowing developers to run agentic code without paying Anthropic or OpenAI. Software chief Craig Federighi said in 2018 that the ergonomics would fatigue users. "We make the world's best touch computer on an iPad," Ternus, then Apple's senior VP of hardware engineering, told The Wall Street Journal in 2021. "It's totally optimized for that. And the Mac is totally optimized for indirect input. We haven't really felt a reason to change that." Ternus has been working on Macs since he joined the company and was credited along with silicon chief Johny Srouji as the leader of Apple's effort to get Macs running on Apple's chips, not Intel's. Apple credited Ternus' work on Mac in its official CEO transition statement . That may be why Ternus in his early days as CEO will be the executive to backtrack on a long-running Apple design philosophy. Touchscreen laptops have been available on Windows machines for a long time, but they're just another feature, not a selling point behind most purchasing decisions, said Ryan Reith, IDC's vice president for worldwide device trackers. Only 17% of notebook PCs shipped globally this year will have touchscreens, according to IDC data. Touchscreen laptops also have a slightly lower average selling price than non-touchscreen notebooks. Hardware technology hasn't been the limiting factor for Apple merging its desktop and mobile interfaces, he added, and Apple could have been waiting to launch a touchscreen laptop until it could present a good user experience and perfect its software after attempts to make its iPad more like a laptop. "This is really a user interface and software thing," Reith said.
